evidence: Abstract: 'an evaluation framework consisting of 2,294 software engineering problems drawn from real GitHub issues'. F->P appears only in Sec 2.1 Stage III: 'We filter out task instances without at least one test where its status changes from a fail to pass'. Abstract says nothing about F->P; 'origin' unsupported (fail-before/pass-after predates it, e.g. Defects4J).
correction: SWE-bench (Jimenez et al., ICLR 2024) builds 2,294 issue tasks from 12 Python repos (Abstract) and keeps only instances with at least one fail-to-pass test, used to evaluate candidate patches (Sec 2.1 Stage III; Sec 2.3 'Robust evaluation'). Drop 'origin of'; say 'popularized F->P evaluation for LLM issue resolution'.

evidence: FAIL_TO_PASS: 'A json list of strings that represent the set of tests resolved by the PR and tied to the issue resolution.' PASS_TO_PASS: 'tests that should pass before and after the PR application.'

Card: 'SWE-bench Verified is a subset of 500 samples from the SWE-bench test set, which have been human-validated for quality.' The card does not itself say the benchmark tests needed validation; it defers to an external post.
correction: Cite card only for '500 human-validated samples'. For the claim that original SWE-bench tests/specs were often flawed, cite OpenAI's 'Introducing SWE-bench Verified' post (Aug 2024) [verify].

evidence: Abstract: 'LIBRO can generate failure reproducing test cases for 33% of all studied cases (251 out of 750)'. Table III: One Example crash bugs reproduced 69; One Example with Stack 84 (Sec VI-A1: 'adding stack traces does help reproduce crash bugs').
correction: Venue: ICSE 2023 (Kang, Yoon, Yoo). Note Table III numbers are summed over n=10 samples, no significance test.

evidence: Sec 3.1: successful 'if it contains at least one F→P test and no ×→F test'; 'We consider a test to fail if an error is thrown during its execution.' Table 2: SWE-Agent+ S=18.5%. Sec 5.3: 'more than doubles the precision of SWE-Agent to 47.8%'.
correction: Metadata: Mündler, Müller, He, Vechev; NeurIPS 2024 (per harness repo description). 47.8% precision comes at ~20% recall.

evidence: Repo description: '[NeurIPS 2024] Evaluation harness for SWT-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM repository-level test-generation'. License MIT; Docker required.
correction: Quote is the GitHub repo description, not README body. 'Runnable baseline' is partial: evaluates any predictions JSONL and ships prior predictions/logs, but no turnkey generation of new baseline predictions.

evidence: Abstract: 'a high-quality benchmark suite of 449 issues mined from real-world GitHub code repositories'; reports fail-to-pass rate and 'high coverage adequacy'.
correction: Metadata: Ahmed, Hirzel, Pan, Shinnar, Sinha (IBM); arXiv preprint Dec 2024, no venue listed.

evidence: README: 'TDD-Bench-Verified is a new benchmark for generating test cases for test-driven development (TDD).' License: Apache-2.0.
